# p0_aws_ssm_ai_connector (Resource)

An AWS SSM (AI) connector installation.

The connector lets P0 give AI agents SSH access to the EC2 instances that SSM manages in its AWS account: for each agent's request it adds the agent's SSH key to an instance, and removes the key when the access ends. It keeps each key in AWS Secrets Manager, in the connector's own account, where the agent's MCP server reads it through AWS OIDC.

**Important:** Before creating this resource you must stage the connector with `p0_aws_ssm_ai_connector_staged`, and set up the following in the staged AWS account and region:

- An IAM role named `p0-connector-aws-ssm-ai` that Lambda can assume, with policies that let it list the instances SSM manages, run the `AWS-RunShellScript` document on them, and manage the agents' secrets in `vault.secrets_region`. That document runs any command as root, so this role can run any command as root on every instance SSM manages in the account. Protect the Lambda and its role as you would root on those instances.
- The `p0-connector-aws-ssm-ai` Lambda, running as that role.
- A policy on P0's AWS IAM management role that allows `lambda:InvokeFunction` on the Lambda.

Every apply that creates or changes this resource has P0 check the install: that it can invoke the Lambda, and that the connector can list the instances SSM manages in each of `instance_regions`. P0 retries for about half a minute while a new IAM policy takes effect. If a check fails, the apply fails with P0's message, and the connector keeps its current values. If the first apply is denied access, apply again.

A connector that P0 hasn't finished installing, such as one imported before its install check passed, plans an update, and applying it finishes the install.

Destroying this resource returns the connector to staged, which P0 refuses once AWS IAM management or AWS OIDC is gone for the account. Keep both until the connector is destroyed, for example with a `depends_on` on the staged resource.

**Note:** This integration is in preview.

For the full install steps, see [AWS SSM MCP server](https://docs.p0.dev/integrations/resource-integrations/agentic-gateway/mcp-server/aws-ssm).

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Installs the AWS SSM (AI) connector: one Lambda per AWS account, outside any VPC,
# that P0 invokes to give AI agents SSH access to the EC2 instances SSM manages
# in that account. It adds and removes each agent's SSH key on an instance
# through SSM, and keeps the key in AWS Secrets Manager in the same account.
# Apply it as an AWS admin of the connector's account.
#
# Before you apply this, install P0's AWS IAM management (see p0_aws_iam_write),
# AWS OIDC (see p0_aws_oidc_identity) and AWS Secrets Manager (see
# p0_aws_secrets_manager) for the connector's AWS account. P0 invokes the
# connector as AWS IAM management's role.

terraform {
  # 1.4 added terraform_data.
  required_version = ">= 1.4"

  required_providers {
    aws = {
      source  = "hashicorp/aws"
      version = ">= 6.0"
    }
    docker = {
      source  = "kreuzwerker/docker"
      version = "~> 3.0"
    }
    # 0.100.0 added the AWS SSM (AI) resources.
    p0 = {
      source  = "p0-security/p0"
      version = ">= 0.100.0"
    }
  }
}

locals {
  account_id = "123456789012"
  region     = "us-east-1"

  # The region the connector keeps every agent's key in. The connector's role
  # may manage secrets in this region only.
  secrets_region = "us-east-1"

  # The connector's name. P0 invokes it by this name, in the account and region
  # above, so keep it as it is. The connector's Lambda function, role, log group
  # and ECR repository all take it.
  connector_name = "p0-connector-aws-ssm-ai"

  # How many days CloudWatch keeps the connector's logs.
  log_retention_days = 30

  # The role that P0's AWS IAM management assumes in this account, which
  # invokes the connector.
  p0_role_name = "P0RoleIamManager"

  # The connector image's version: the sha- tag P0 publishes each release
  # under, and the digest that tag must resolve to. Docker Hub lets a tag be
  # pushed again, so the plan fails if the tag no longer resolves to this
  # digest. To update, take both from the latest version of this example in
  # the Terraform registry: they change together. Changing them copies the
  # image again and redeploys the Lambda.
  connector_image_name   = "p0security/p0-connector-aws-ssm-ai"
  connector_image_tag    = "sha-d303c79"
  connector_image_digest = "sha256:0113d187207289254bae1f11abb6914091a6ce82224b35ec99597a8eac9bc141"

  tags = {
    ManagedBy  = "Terraform"
    ManagedFor = "P0"
  }
}

provider "aws" {
  region              = local.region
  allowed_account_ids = [local.account_id]
}

# Staging records the connector in P0 before the Lambda is deployed.
resource "p0_aws_ssm_ai_connector_staged" "example" {
  id     = local.account_id
  region = local.region
  vault = {
    type           = "aws-sm"
    account_id     = local.account_id
    secrets_region = local.secrets_region
  }

  # Destroying the connector needs AWS IAM management and AWS OIDC. If this
  # configuration installs them, depend on them, so that Terraform destroys
  # the connector first.
  # depends_on = [p0_aws_iam_write.example, p0_aws_oidc_identity.example]
}

# The connector's execution role, which may do only what the policies below
# allow.
resource "aws_iam_role" "connector" {
  name = local.connector_name
  tags = local.tags
  assume_role_policy = jsonencode({
    Version = "2012-10-17"
    Statement = [{
      Effect    = "Allow"
      Principal = { Service = "lambda.amazonaws.com" }
      Action    = "sts:AssumeRole"
    }]
  })
}

# The log group Lambda writes the connector's logs to.
resource "aws_cloudwatch_log_group" "connector" {
  name              = "/aws/lambda/${local.connector_name}"
  retention_in_days = local.log_retention_days
  tags              = local.tags
}

# The connector writes its own logs, and no others.
resource "aws_iam_role_policy" "connector_logs" {
  name = "${local.connector_name}-logs"
  role = aws_iam_role.connector.id
  policy = jsonencode({
    Version = "2012-10-17"
    Statement = [{
      Effect   = "Allow"
      Action   = ["logs:CreateLogStream", "logs:PutLogEvents"]
      Resource = "${aws_cloudwatch_log_group.connector.arn}:*"
    }]
  })
}

# The connector lists the instances SSM manages in this account, with their
# Name tags, lists and follows the commands it sends, and ends an agent's
# SSM sessions when its access ends.
resource "aws_iam_role_policy" "connector_instances" {
  name = "${local.connector_name}-instances"
  role = aws_iam_role.connector.id
  policy = jsonencode({
    Version = "2012-10-17"
    Statement = [{
      Effect = "Allow"
      Action = [
        "ec2:DescribeTags",
        "ssm:DescribeInstanceInformation",
        "ssm:DescribeSessions",
        "ssm:GetCommandInvocation",
        "ssm:ListCommands",
        "ssm:TerminateSession",
      ]
      Resource  = "*"
      Condition = { StringEquals = { "aws:ResourceAccount" = local.account_id } }
    }]
  })
}

# The connector adds and removes agents' keys by sending a script through the
# AWS-RunShellScript document, to any instance in this account, in any region.
# That document runs any command as root, so this role can run any command as
# root on every instance SSM manages in this account. Nothing in AWS holds it
# to the connector's own script, so protect the Lambda and this role as you
# would root on those instances.
resource "aws_iam_role_policy" "connector_run_script" {
  name = "${local.connector_name}-run-script"
  role = aws_iam_role.connector.id
  policy = jsonencode({
    Version = "2012-10-17"
    Statement = [{
      Effect = "Allow"
      Action = "ssm:SendCommand"
      Resource = [
        "arn:aws:ssm:*::document/AWS-RunShellScript",
        "arn:aws:ec2:*:${local.account_id}:instance/*",
      ]
    }]
  })
}

# The connector keeps each agent's key in a secret of its own, all in the
# secrets region above. It may create, look up, write and delete those
# secrets, and no others. It can't read one back: the agent's MCP server reads
# its key through AWS OIDC.
resource "aws_iam_role_policy" "connector_grant_secrets" {
  name = "${local.connector_name}-grant-secrets"
  role = aws_iam_role.connector.id
  policy = jsonencode({
    Version = "2012-10-17"
    Statement = [{
      Effect = "Allow"
      Action = [
        "secretsmanager:CreateSecret",
        "secretsmanager:DeleteSecret",
        "secretsmanager:DescribeSecret",
        "secretsmanager:PutSecretValue",
      ]
      Resource = "arn:aws:secretsmanager:${local.secrets_region}:${local.account_id}:secret:p0/access-token/aws-ssm-ai/${local.account_id}/*"
    }]
  })
}

data "docker_registry_image" "connector" {
  name = "${local.connector_image_name}:${local.connector_image_tag}"

  lifecycle {
    postcondition {
      condition     = self.sha256_digest == local.connector_image_digest
      error_message = "The connector image's tag doesn't resolve to the digest pinned here. Take both from the latest p0_aws_ssm_ai_connector example in P0's Terraform registry docs, or contact support@p0.dev."
    }
  }
}

# Lambda only runs images from Amazon ECR, so this copies P0's image into a
# repository in this account. It needs docker and the AWS CLI, signed in to this
# account, wherever Terraform runs.
resource "aws_ecr_repository" "connector" {
  name = local.connector_name
  # Tags can't be overwritten, so no one who can push to this repository can
  # replace the image that runs as the execution role.
  image_tag_mutability = "IMMUTABLE"
  force_delete         = true
  tags                 = local.tags

  image_scanning_configuration {
    scan_on_push = true
  }
}

# Copies the pinned image again whenever its tag or digest changes, tagged
# with the image's tag and this copy's id. ECR's tags can't be overwritten, so
# each copy needs a tag of its own: copying the image again, to roll back or
# after an interrupted apply, pushes a new one.
resource "terraform_data" "connector_image" {
  triggers_replace = {
    digest         = data.docker_registry_image.connector.sha256_digest
    repository_url = aws_ecr_repository.connector.repository_url
    tag            = local.connector_image_tag
  }

  provisioner "local-exec" {
    # Signs Docker out of ECR at the end, so its login doesn't outlast the copy.
    # A failed sign-out doesn't fail the copy once the image is pushed.
    command = <<-EOT
      set -e
      trap 'docker logout "$REGISTRY" || true' EXIT
      aws ecr get-login-password --region "$REGION" |
        docker login --username AWS --password-stdin "$REGISTRY"
      docker pull --platform linux/amd64 "$SOURCE"
      docker tag "$SOURCE" "$TARGET"
      docker push "$TARGET"
    EOT

    environment = {
      REGION   = local.region
      REGISTRY = split("/", aws_ecr_repository.connector.repository_url)[0]
      SOURCE   = "${local.connector_image_name}@${local.connector_image_digest}"
      TARGET   = "${aws_ecr_repository.connector.repository_url}:${local.connector_image_tag}-${self.id}"
    }
  }
}

# Pulling one platform and pushing it can give ECR a different manifest from
# the one the tag names on Docker Hub, so the digest there can differ from the
# one pinned above. Lambda needs ECR's.
data "aws_ecr_image" "connector" {
  repository_name = aws_ecr_repository.connector.name
  image_tag       = "${local.connector_image_tag}-${terraform_data.connector_image.id}"
}

resource "aws_lambda_function" "connector" {
  # P0 invokes the connector by its name in this account and region, so it must
  # be deployed exactly there. If your other AWS providers have credential
  # settings, such as profile or assume_role, add them to the provider above.
  function_name = local.connector_name
  role          = aws_iam_role.connector.arn
  package_type  = "Image"
  image_uri     = "${aws_ecr_repository.connector.repository_url}@${data.aws_ecr_image.connector.image_digest}"
  architectures = ["x86_64"]
  memory_size   = 512
  # P0 holds a 60-second lock around a whole grant, which makes several
  # connector calls, so no call may take longer.
  timeout = 60
  tags    = local.tags

  # The connector is staged in P0 before it's deployed. Its role can't create
  # a log group, so its own must exist before it runs.
  depends_on = [
    p0_aws_ssm_ai_connector_staged.example,
    aws_cloudwatch_log_group.connector,
  ]
}

# Lets P0 invoke the connector, through the role P0's AWS IAM management
# assumes in this account.
resource "aws_iam_role_policy" "p0_invoke_connector" {
  name = "${local.connector_name}-invoke"
  role = local.p0_role_name
  policy = jsonencode({
    Version = "2012-10-17"
    Statement = [{
      Effect   = "Allow"
      Action   = "lambda:InvokeFunction"
      Resource = aws_lambda_function.connector.arn
    }]
  })
}

# Completes the install. P0 checks that it can invoke the connector, retrying
# for about half a minute while a new IAM policy takes effect, and that the
# connector can list the instances SSM manages in each instance region. If the
# first apply is denied access, apply again.
resource "p0_aws_ssm_ai_connector" "example" {
  id     = p0_aws_ssm_ai_connector_staged.example.id
  region = p0_aws_ssm_ai_connector_staged.example.region
  vault  = p0_aws_ssm_ai_connector_staged.example.vault

  # The regions whose instances agents can request.
  instance_regions = ["us-east-1", "us-west-2"]

  # The Linux users that agents can ask to run as. An agent signs in as its
  # own Linux user, then switches with sudo. Leave it out to let agents run
  # only as themselves.
  run_as_users = ["root"]

  depends_on = [
    aws_iam_role_policy.connector_instances,
    aws_iam_role_policy.connector_run_script,
    aws_iam_role_policy.connector_grant_secrets,
    aws_iam_role_policy.p0_invoke_connector,
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `id` (String) The ID of the AWS account that the connector's Lambda runs in. P0 reaches every instance that SSM manages in this account through the connector.
- `instance_regions` (List of String) The AWS regions whose instances agents can request, such as `["us-west-2", "us-east-1"]`. Each must be a commercial AWS region, listed once. P0 checks that the connector can list the instances SSM manages in each. Changing it updates the connector in place, and P0 checks the install again.
- `region` (String) The AWS region that the connector's Lambda runs in. The connector runs only in commercial AWS regions.
- `vault` (Attributes) The secret manager where the connector keeps each agent's SSH key, as installed in P0. The connector writes each key, and the agent's MCP server reads it through AWS OIDC, only in the connector's own AWS account, so this must be that account's AWS Secrets Manager installation. Changing it replaces the connector. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--vault))

### Optional

- `is_sudo_enabled` (Boolean, Deprecated) Use `run_as_users` instead. `true` lets agents run as `root`, as `run_as_users = ["root"]` does. Defaults to `false`. It can't be set with `run_as_users`. Changing it updates the connector in place.
- `run_as_users` (List of String) The Linux users that agents can ask to run as on an instance, such as `["root", "deploy"]`. Each must be a Linux user name, listed once. An agent always signs in as its own Linux user, then switches to the user it asked for with `sudo`. Leave it out to let agents run only as their own users. P0 refuses requests for any user not listed. Changing it updates the connector in place.

### Read-Only

- `state` (String) This item's install progress in the P0 application:
	- 'stage': The item has been staged for installation
	- 'configure': The item is available to be added to P0, and may be configured
	- 'installed': The item is fully installed

<a id="nestedatt--vault"></a>
### Nested Schema for `vault`

Required:

- `account_id` (String) The ID of the AWS account whose AWS Secrets Manager installation in P0 (`p0_aws_secrets_manager`) keeps the keys. It must be the connector's `id`.
- `secrets_region` (String) The AWS region the connector keeps every key in, such as `us-west-2`. It must be a commercial AWS region. The connector's role may manage secrets in this region only.
- `type` (String) The secret manager. The only value is `aws-sm` (AWS Secrets Manager).
